source.title: Towards Interpretable Framework for Neural Audio Codecs via Sparse Autoencoders: Exploration toward Age, Gender, and Accent Steering
source.authors: Shi Wang; Tian-Tian Feng; Aditya Kommineni; Huang-Cheng Chou; Bo-Wen Yi; Xuan Shi; Shrikanth S. Narayanan

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; some equations and figure contents are rendered imperfectly, but the paper is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SAE dimensions in neural audio codecs encode steerable speaker-trait information. Its reported quality and content degradation qualifies the idea that SAE features fully isolate trait information, though it does not test superposition geometry or capacity pressure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE steering outcomes and collateral speech-quality outcomes. The selected-dimension counts and hyperparameters are setup choices, not results. Figure-only outcomes are recorded as such; the accompanying text gives the qualitative direction. The random-dimension comparison on Mimi is an outcome and is included.
record.test_reason: The study uses Top-k SAEs as a tool to probe speaker-trait information in neural audio codecs. It reports how well its own dimension-selection and steering procedure works: trait shifts, a random-dimension control, and WER/quality costs. It never tests superposition geometry, capacity pressure, neuron polysemanticity, LLM feature spread, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical. The authors blame the quality degradation on 'the selected activations and steering procedure' together. So it is a performance result for their method, not a test of V5. The systems are audio codecs, not LLMs, so V4 does not apply either.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say SAE steering produces target-directed trait shifts across five codecs, with variable responses and inconsistent gains from larger α. They say content and quality degradation means the SAE does not fully isolate speaker traits, and call for better SAE optimization.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Top-k SAEs and activation-frequency-based dimension selection followed by activation steering in neural audio codecs; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across codec, trait, steering direction, and steering strength; increasing α does not consistently strengthen the intended shift.

fits_no_version.finding: In five neural audio codecs, steering about 30 activation-frequency-selected Top-k SAE dimensions per group shifts predicted gender, age and accent in the target direction, unevenly by codec, trait and direction. Random dimensions in Mimi shift less. Steering generally raises WER and lowers SHEET quality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in non-LLM (audio codec) representations carry steerable trait information but do not cleanly isolate it from content and quality information.

record.problems: Steering outcomes and quality metrics are shown in figures without numerical values in the text. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Trait-associated dimensions are selected using labeled test waveforms, which the authors say is allowed under their setup; this does not test whether the dimensions are stable or canonical.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome relevant to V5 was left out. Other versions are not tested; the paper’s remaining results do not test the versions’ claims.

untested.parts: No toy models, overlap geometry, or sparsity transition.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No LLMs studied; SAE recovery is not evaluated as evidence of superposition.
Completeness, stability across runs, and canonicality of SAE features are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/V5 limits_scope label is dropped. The rows measure the performance of the study's own steering method, not V5's completeness, stability or canonicality, and the degradation is confounded with the steering procedure (zeroing and ±α on Top-k active dimensions). All outcomes are figure-only, with no uncertainty reported. Dimensions were selected on labelled test data.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not studied.
The study does not test neuron polysemanticity or feature competition for limited capacity.
The study does not examine polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of neuron polysemanticity.
The models are neural audio codecs, not LLMs; the study does not measure feature spread across LLM neurons or LLM SAE recovery.

Tests whether SAE dimensions encode steerable speaker-trait information and how well they separate it from other speech information in neural audio codecs. Does not test feature stability across runs or conditions, canonicality, or completeness of the full model representation.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features, or test of superposition geometry.

rows.note: Aggregate qualitative statement; no per-codec numeric values are legible in the text.
rows.check: Measures steerability of gender via selected SAE dimensions (method performance). It does not test completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features. Figure-only.

conditions.value: varied; exact plotted values not stated

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Speaker-trait steering and quality/content evaluation in the five tested neural audio codecs
reader_labels.reason: The selected SAE dimensions produce target-directed trait shifts, but increased WER and reduced SHEET scores indicate that they do not fully isolate trait information from other speech information (r1-r9). Stability and canonicality were not evaluated.
